title: Advanced Reusable Workflow Configuration knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Advanced Reusable Workflow Configuration?
options: Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
Reusable workflow calls need explicit version references, appropriate trust and access, controlled permission/secrets passing, and documented interfaces.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
questions.answer_key: Reusable workflow calls need explicit version references, appropriate trust and access, controlled permission/secrets passing, and documented interfaces.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of advanced reusable workflow configuration: Reusable workflow calls need explicit version references, appropriate trust and access, controlled permission/secrets passing, and documented interfaces. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: A team is working with “Reusing workflows from the same repository”. Which practice best fits this topic?
options: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
questions.answer_key: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action.
questions.explanation: Reusing workflows from the same repository: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action. Apply the guidance to the actual event, runner, permissions, or artifact boundary and test the relevant case.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to advanced reusable workflow configuration?
options: Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: Reusable workflow calls need explicit version references, appropriate trust and access, controlled permission/secrets passing, and documented interfaces. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
